title: Simplify a File Path
constraints: path starts with `/` and contains only letters, dots and slashes

examples.explanation: The double slash counts as one and the trailing slash is removed.
/a/./b becomes /a/b; the first .. goes back to /a; the second .. goes back to /; then /c.

hints.nudge: Going up with `..` undoes the most recent step down. What structure undoes the most recent thing?
hints.pattern: A stack of folder names: split the path at the slashes, skip empty parts and `.`, pop for `..`, push everything else.
hints.pseudocode:
stack = empty
for part in path split at '/':
  if part is empty or '.': continue
  if part is '..': pop if the stack is not empty
  else: push part
return '/' + the stack joined by '/'
hints.walkthrough: Cut the path into the pieces between slashes. Empty pieces come from repeated or trailing slashes and carry no information; a piece `.` changes nothing. A piece `..` removes the last folder that you went into, so keep the folders you are currently inside on a stack: pop when you meet `..` (and do nothing if you are already at the top: the stack is empty). Any other piece is a folder (or file) name: push it. Only the pieces that are exactly `.` or `..` are special: names like `..hidden` are pushed. At the end join the stack with slashes and put one `/` in front; an empty stack gives just `/`. O(n).
